title: fanoutqa: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations. (ca085ff48e269f74)

chat_history.content: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations.

content.content:
User asks: Identify the US presidents who served two terms and their political affiliations. Should list all presidents who served two full terms (i.e., elected twice). Need to include those who served two terms (including non-consecutive? Actually two terms means served two terms, could be consecutive or non-consecutive? Typically "served two terms" means two full terms, could be non-consecutive like Grover Cleveland (served two non-consecutive terms). Should include him.

List: George Washington (no party), Thomas Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), James Madison (Democratic-Republican), James Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Andrew Jackson (Democratic), Ulysses S. Grant (Republican), Grover Cleveland (Democratic) though non-consecutive, Woodrow Wilson (Democratic), Dwight D. Eisenhower (Republican), Ronald Reagan (Republican), Bill Clinton (Democratic), George W. Bush (Republican), Barack Obama (Democratic), and maybe also: James K. Polk served one term. So also: William McKinley (assassinated early 2nd). Not full term? He was elected twice but died early in second term; still considered two-term? Usually "served two terms" implies completed two terms, but some lists include those who were elected to two terms even if didn't complete second. But safe to list those who served two full terms.

Let's compile: Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, Jackson, Grant, Cleveland, Wilson, Eisenhower, Reagan, Clinton, Bush (George W.), Obama. Also: Thomas Jefferson? Yes. Also: James K. Polk no. Also: William McKinley died early; not full.

Also: Franklin D. Roosevelt served more than two terms (four). Not included.

Also: Harry S. Truman served a partial term then elected one term (so not two). Not included.

Also: Dwight D. Eisenhower is Republican.

Also: Ronald Reagan Republican.

Also: Bill Clinton Democrat.

Also: George W. Bush Republican.

Also: Barack Obama Democrat.

Also: maybe include: James Madison (Democratic-Republican).

Also: James Monroe (Democratic-Republican).

Also: Andrew Jackson (Democratic).

Also: Ulysses S. Grant (Republican).

Also: Grover Cleveland (Democratic) – non-consecutive.

Also: Woodrow Wilson (Democratic).

Also: maybe include: William Howard Taft served one term.

Thus answer.

Provide list with years and party.

Will produce bullet list.

content:
**U.S. Presidents who completed two full terms (including the non‑consecutive case of Grover Cleveland) and their political parties**

| President | Years in Office (two terms) | Political Party |
|-----------|----------------------------|-----------------|
| **George Washington** | 1789‑1797 | No formal party (often described as “Federalist‑leaning”) |
| **Thomas Jefferson** | 1801‑1809 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **James Madison** | 1809‑1817 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **James Monroe** | 1817‑1825 | Democratic‑Republican |
| **Andrew Jackson** | 1829‑1837 | Democratic |
| **Ulysses S. Grant** | 1869‑1877 | Republican |
| **Grover Cleveland** *(non‑consecutive)* | 1885‑1889 & 1893‑1897 | Democratic |
| **Woodrow Wilson** | 1913‑1921 | Democratic |
| **Dwight D. Eisenhower** | 1953‑1961 | Republican |
| **Ronald Reagan** | 1981‑1989 | Republican |
| **Bill Clinton** | 1993‑2001 | Democratic |
| **George W. Bush** | 2001‑2009 | Republican |
| **Barack Obama** | 2009‑2017 | Democratic |

### Notes

* **George Washington** never identified with a party; the modern party system had not yet formed.  
* **Grover Cleveland** is the only president to serve two terms that were not consecutive (22nd and 24th President).  
* Presidents who were elected twice but did **not** complete a second full term (e.g., William McKinley, who was assassinated early in his second term) are excluded from this list.  
* Franklin D. Roosevelt, who won four elections, is also excluded because the question asks for presidents who served **two** terms.  

These are the leaders who have been elected to, and completed, two full four‑year terms in the history of the United States.
